> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebb4713c06f06adbfe0390b5722c70e31948e3a1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c72661e2077f3b99c2d0273ccd25e6226697dde0` — the merge of head `46266e8a062ed1837bf429ca51cbd65eede07397` into base `ebb4713c06f06adbfe0390b5722c70e31948e3a1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c72661e2077f3b99c2d0273ccd25e6226697dde0 && git checkout c72661e2077f3b99c2d0273ccd25e6226697dde0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ebb4713c06f06adbfe0390b5722c70e31948e3a1 46266e8a062ed1837bf429ca51cbd65eede07397 && git checkout -B drift-repro ebb4713c06f06adbfe0390b5722c70e31948e3a1 && git merge --no-ff 46266e8a062ed1837bf429ca51cbd65eede07397

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebb4713c06f06adbfe0390b5722c70e31948e3a1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ebb4713c06f06adbfe0390b5722c70e31948e3a1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · L1 · head `53f2e69c8bc0f59a9420fc52c4c944f45b77fb36` · 2026-11-24T19:14Z

Read against GitHub and the tree at this head: card #36991 and its 3 comments, epic #37000's binding rules, the zone's finalized-head note (7141528526), PR #36850's merged gates, and the full diff (6 files, +612/−150, merge-base `8aecf6d770`).

D1 (should-fix) — Three new texts say the event-path document carries "only the fields the source lists": `knowledge.mdx` §6 ("The same field rules as a reindex apply: only the fields the source lists, and never a credential-class or `internal` field"), the changeset ("only the fields the source lists; credential-class and `internal` fields never") and the `handleRecordUpsert` JSDoc ("only the fields the source lists"). The PR body's first bullet says the same. `recordToDocument` (unchanged here, shared with `reindexSource`) also sets the document `title` from `record.title` whenever it is a string and not withheld, whether or not the source lists `title`. §5 of the same page already names it ("every `contentFields` member of its source, the record `title` and the source's `metadataFields`"). Reword all four places to match, for example "the fields the source lists and the record `title`, never a credential-class or `internal` field". The behaviour itself is unchanged and stays as it is.

D2 (should-fix) — The rollback sentence covers only one of its two outcomes. In `knowledge.mdx` §6, the `handleRecordUpsert` JSDoc and the changeset ("a rolled-back write leaves its document until …"), it says the document "stays built from a row that never committed". On the miss branch, the re-read inside the uncommitted unit finds no match and deletes the document. A rollback then leaves the committed, still-matching row out of the index until its next event or a `reindexSource`. That is a new rollback outcome of this PR's re-read, a missing document where the payload path left wrong text. It is not worse, but it needs its own sentence. Name both outcomes. The phase-4 card that the zone's note (7141528526) files at ACCEPT should carry both as well.

S1 (nit) — The per-document chain is awaited inline, so one request's write can wait on another request's in-flight sync of the same document. On a single-connection pool (SQLite), a sync whose re-read runs outside any transaction (a write with no unit of its own, or `data.record.restored`, published after commit) can sit waiting for the connection. Meanwhile a second request's transaction on the same row holds that connection and waits on the chain. The wait lasts until the pool's acquire timeout. The earlier sync then fails with a warn, and the later re-read still leaves the index correct. The window is narrow, the state ends consistent, and the phase-4 queue removes the inline wait. One sentence in §6 ("a write's sync can wait behind an earlier sync of the same document") or a line on that phase-4 card is enough. A code change is not asked for in this round.

### Checklist readings

- **Shape and card:** `l1-face.mjs --pr 37075` is CLEAN at `53f2e69c8b` (13 items). The PR is draft, based on `main`, with first line `Fixes #36991`, and no closing keyword binds any other card. `Fixes` is right because all six What items are delivered. Items 1 and 2: re-read by `where ∧ id`, `limit: 1`, system context; a hit builds via `recordToDocument` + `schemaFor`, a miss deletes. Item 3: `RECORD_RESTORED_EVENT` is in the bridge, and its comment and the `enableEventSync` docs now name all four events. Item 4: with no engine, a source without `where` builds from the payload; a source with `where` is skipped with one warn per source. Item 5: per-document chain. Item 6: ordering stated in the code comment and §6, and the bulk callout is kept. All eight Acceptance tests are present in `event-sync-data-events.test.ts`, the file is rewritten, and the container counts are in the PR body. Out of scope is held: no adapter-contract member, no organization ids, no queue.
- **Scope, changeset, declarations:** all 6 files are within the claim's file surface. `@objectstack/service-knowledge` is at `patch`, which is right for a bug fix with no signature change. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the body and the changeset, and they agree with the diff (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no authorable key). Nothing under `content/docs/releases/`. Skills-docs is not owed.
- **Contract-review face:** none. `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths <6 files>` reports that the paths decide no face, and it defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line. That line is `no`, with no `(narrowing)` arm. So no declaration face and no L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` or `TIER_DEFAULT` is owed.
- **Gates:** check-runs at `53f2e69c8b`: 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are `success`. `mergeable_state` is `clean`. Dogfood is not owed (no `!`, no narrowing).
- **Test evidence:** real commands with output: 117/117 package tests (event-sync 23, knowledge-service 28), typecheck exit 0, dependency closure built first. Four ablations through `ablation-replace.mjs`, each with an anchor that hit 1 then 0 and a restore to HEAD: `where`→`{ id }` 5/23 red, serialisation removed 3/23, restored dropped 2/23, payload instead of the re-read row 3/51. The engine double refuses any operator it does not implement, so a query shape it cannot answer turns the suite red.
- **Serialisation:** the map key is `${source.id}:${recordId}` for both upsert and delete. Each sync runs after the previous one settles and re-reads on its own, so a later sync never acts on an earlier read. The `catch` keeps a rejected task from breaking the chain. The tail removes itself in `finally` only while it is still the stored tail, so the map holds only in-flight documents. `whereUnenforceableReported` is bounded by the source count. Ordering holds within one process only, as the docs and the PR body say. For the cross-request wait, see S1.
- **Tenant and organisation scope:** the re-read uses `systemContext()`, the same isSystem context as the reindex walk, and carries no organisation scope. It is keyed by the event's own record id, so it reads only the row the event names. That is no wider than the payload it replaces or than `reindexSource`, and search still re-checks each hit as the caller.
- **PR #36850 gates:** `recordToDocument` withholding applies to the re-read row, pinned under `'*'` and under named fields in `knowledge-service.test.ts`. `admitSources` is search-time, and the event path does not reach or skip it.
- **Egress:** the event path sends exactly what `reindexSource` sends for the same row. Under `'*'` that is every string field of the row, per the seat's routing (option A); retiring `'*'` is epic row 3. For the wording, see D1.
- **Rollback staleness:** documented in the code comment and §6. Not worsened, but incompletely stated (D2).
- **Docs sentences checked against the code:**
  - The `data.record.*` wording at :55.
  - The four-event vocabulary, and that a bare `record.*` is ignored. The bridge has no branch for it, and tests pin it.
  - The re-read query shape.
  - Hit builds from the re-read row and cannot be short.
  - Miss deletes. Deleting an absent document is a no-op in both in-repo adapters (`knowledge-memory` filters; `knowledge-ragflow` deletes what it finds).
  - Restored row takes the same path.
  - Both no-engine branches.
  - Delete by `recordId`.
  - Per-process serialisation.
  - Created/updated published inside the write after the `after*` hooks, and before the unit or caller transaction commits. Verified at `engine-insert.ts`, `engine-update.ts` and `engine-realtime-publish.ts:484`.
  - The in-memory realtime adapter awaits each subscriber (`in-memory-realtime-adapter.ts:98`).
  - Restored is published after the restore's own unit (`restore.ts:470`, `:756`).
  - The changeset's bullets were read the same way.
  - Exceptions: D1 and D2.

### Rework

A patch round on the same claim, text only: D1 in four places (mdx §6, changeset, JSDoc, PR body) and D2 in three (mdx §6, JSDoc, changeset). S1 is optional. Re-run the package tests and post the new head.
